```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Willingness to pay is better evidenced in A. Published competitor pricing of $99/provider/month (ClaireMed) and $99–$500 (S10.AI) shows the actual payer, the physician, paying for this category. In B, the reachable self-serve segment has at least four competitors with free or low tiers. B's own brief says this pushes pricing toward zero.",
    "A's precedent shows a first paying customer is achievable, even though it also shows scaling is hard. Cydoc landed four paying customers and its first sales call revealed demand specifically for note drafting. A's proposed narrowing (intake-to-note draft pasted into the existing EHR, no custom integration) answers the $4–6k integration cost that sank Cydoc. The question here is one paying customer in 90 days, not a durable business.",
    "B's only payer channel that fits 90 days is self-serve developers, which the brief says is crowded and near-free. Its high-value channel, banks, requires SOC 2 Type II and 6–18 month cycles. B's own case against concedes that banks are incompatible with the timeline.",
    "Both ideas carry regulatory overhead, but A's is routine for small customers: per-customer BAAs and a one-time FDA non-device review. B faces open-ended biometric exposure. The brief cites BIPA's $650M settlement and Worldcoin bans, and leaves unresolved whether any signal in the design triggers BIPA or GDPR biometric obligations.",
    "A's demand evidence is also weak. The PMHNP Reddit quote is about intake paperwork, not an AI note tool, and the AMA statistic comes secondhand via competitor marketing. The edge for A rests mainly on competitor pricing and the Cydoc paying-customer record, not on direct buyer quotes."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "The Trevor Traina quote ('establishing trust online becomes essential') is a promotional statement from a competitor's Chief Business Officer announcing his own company's partnership. It shows no buyer pain or willingness to pay from any platform a solo founder could sell to. B's other demand items are also indirect. The r/OnlineDating quote comes from an end user, not the paying platform, and the $243K deepfake wire concerns banks, which B admits are unreachable in the timeframe.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-low confidence. A is a well-documented hard market. Cydoc's founder had clinical credentials and still earned only $27.9K in 2024, and A's acquisition channel (conference booths at $1,850–$10,000) is costly for a solo operator. B wins on cheap acquisition but loses on payer willingness to pay and on feasible channels. Neither brief contains direct evidence of a paying-customer conversation in the proposed narrowed form. Both briefs reference a six-week build rather than the 90-day goal."
}
```
